description.short_caption: Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid showing gram-negative diplococci.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid. Numerous gram-negative diplococci are visible, appearing as paired, pink-staining cocci. The background is lightly stained, consistent with a spun preparation of cerebrospinal fluid. The morphology and staining characteristics suggest a bacterial pathogen, potentially Neisseria species.
visible_findings: lightly stained background typical of cerebrospinal fluid preparation

description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain with numerous pink-staining (gram-negative) diplococci visible against a lighter background. The organisms are arranged in pairs and are surrounded by inflammatory cells, suggesting an infectious process. The staining technique highlights the characteristic morphology of the bacteria.

Case_04004/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3. Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid, high power.

description.short_caption: Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid showing Gram-negative diplococci.
description.detailed_description: This high-power Gram stain image shows numerous polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) with intracellular and extracellular Gram-negative diplococci. The organisms are pink, consistent with their Gram-negative staining properties. The background is lightly stained, and the focus is on the central cluster of diplococci. This finding is suggestive of bacterial meningitis, potentially caused by Neisseria meningitidis.
